correctness.rationale: In characteristic 2 the three off-diagonal derivatives vanish and Euler's formula puts the cubic in the ideal of the three principal minors. On a≠0 write x=b/a, y=d/a, η=f/a+xy; the chart is exactly k[x,y,η]/(η²). The three diagonal charts cover since the diagonal equations force all entries to vanish if a=c=e=0. The reduced charts are the Veronese charts. On the two overlaps with a≠0 the other nilpotent generators become x^−3η and y^−3η, the transition laws of O_P²(−3); the local algebra splittings give no global splitting. Independently the graded quotient is free over k[a,c,e] on the eight monomials b^i d^j f^l with i,j,l∈{0,1}, by the three monic square equations. This gives dimension 3 and the Hilbert series (1+t)^3/(1−t)^3, hence the height-three complete intersection, degree 8 and Hilbert polynomial 4n²+2; the degree-four Veronese is its support. The coefficient ac+b² of e is irreducible and cannot divide the constant term af²+cd² (check after localizing at a), so the cubic is irreducible. The complete hypersurface satisfies S₂, and its singular support of dimension 2 in dimension 4 gives R₁ and normality. These chart substitutions and the graded free basis are a replay path for the claimed geometry.
